strengths: One runner for every table: `judge` (bridge-guards.mjs:1780-1827) asks prepare, the sender Foundry names (`senderOf`, 61-64), the guards in order, the whitelist (`pick`, 1526-1535) and the roll records, and only then acknowledges and runs; a throw anywhere ends as one `failed` refusal, never a silent ack.

A result is the GMs' record of its roll, not the packet's: `rollsFor` judges every named roll before it claims any (1674-1678), marks them in memory with nothing awaited between the last question and the last mark, and on the record for a GM who takes over; a packet number that differs is logged and never used (`onRecord`, 1687-1703).
The packet never writes to the shared packet object (the runner's note 1738-1747), and every run is handed a fresh whitelisted copy: `as.gmFlag` (1516) makes a player's `undo` false whatever it says.

Refusals travel as a code of a closed list only (REASONS, REASON_PATTERNS, `tellRefused` clamps an unknown code to `refused`, 530), composed in the player's language on the player's own client (`sayNotDone`, 581-596), so nothing the GM worked out reaches a refused player; all 81 codes have a sentence in both languages.

The waiter resolves once and never rejects (`createWaiter`, 1905-2091), keeps a closed map so a late ack, done or refusal is never said twice, and is built from injected parts so R165 drives it with fakes; `WINDOW_CLOCK` (1891) records the real-browser `setTimeout` receiver failure of 14.10.2026 with its date.

Resends carry the same request id and are bounded (`RESENDS = 3`, 2102); the primary's arrival is the GM-ready packet, not `userConnected` (gm-bridge.mjs:103-111, measured on a live reload), and only the primary's arrival triggers it (COMM-05's fix, gm-bridge.mjs:84-89).

Asked again, answered as before: `again` (bridge-guards.mjs:1795-1807, sabotageAgain bridge-runs-records.mjs:355-360) answers a resent Sabotage with its first result, keyed by Foundry's sender, instead of refusing the roll it settled.

A Hope Call that waits for a GM's yes is armed only with a yes the primary kept for that user, character, Call and nonce, within a minute, once (`guardArmGmYes`, 1122-1132), and a yes whose receipt never came is taken back (`forgetCallYes`).

The player's road of `call.arm` pays from the Hope the GMs hold inside the buyer's audit queue (`gmMeansWrite`, bridge-runs-records.mjs:582-587) and refunds if the arm throws (591-595); a replayed purchase is answered by its nonce, not charged twice (572).
Every row a student's character asks through names `notSpectator` or `senderNotSpectator` right after `knownSender`, read on the flags as the GMs hold them (bridge-guards.mjs:1442-1478).

The share of a secret project asks `canSee` again in the run with nothing awaited between it and the write (prepare imports projects.mjs, bridge-table.mjs:776-778; handleShare bridge-runs-records.mjs:95-96).
Crisis packets that name no roll are scored on no dice, and a `free` claim is believed only when the incident on the GM holds the grant (bridge-runs-acts.mjs:804-846).
A Dynamic action's band reads only a ruling a GM wrote (`dynamicRulingOf` with `cardWriter(...).isGM`, bridge-runs-records.mjs:261-271).
The wire names are a leaf (bridge-wire.mjs imports config.mjs alone) so the table, runs and asks share them without a static cycle (the E41 C5a note, 10-17).

findings.title: Echoes is answered on the primary with no sight of its one-action price, so a player's console asks it free and as often as it likes; a parked murder and a betrayal in an Eclipse are carried out the same way
findings.where: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:277-284 (`listen.echoes`: knownSender, notSpectator, guardUndoIsTheGms, owns; no ticket); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:327-334 (handleEchoes); scripts/echoes-gm.mjs:95-127 (echoesRefusal, echoesFor: no payment read); scripts/action-listen.mjs:317-320 (the action is spent on the asker's browser before requestEchoes); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:870-879 and 892-904 with scripts/action-murder.mjs:285 and 369 (park and betrayal, paid on the asker's browser)
findings.what_happens: Echoes costs one action (config.mjs:2196 `INFILTRATE.echoes.cost: 1`), paid by `spendAction` on the asking player's browser (action-listen.mjs:318-319), and the primary answers `listen.echoes` from the GMs' reading of the map with no question about that payment: no ticket is claimed (roll-draw.mjs `claimTicket`, which an open Frisk's ask claims for exactly this shape of no-roll paid act, frisk.mjs:797-802), and the action count is not read. A console that calls `requestEchoes({ actorId })` (or emits the packet) is answered every time. Each answer is the GMs' knowledge: the nearest room by crossings holding a living student of another player, with the dead as the GMs hold them (including a death nobody has found) and hidden tokens left out; ties are broken at random per ask (echoes-gm.mjs:45), so repeated asks walk every tied room. `murder.park` and `murder.betrayal` in an Eclipse are the same shape - one action on the asker's browser, a declaration written on the primary with no payment read - but they are one-shot declarations, so the cost there is one free action, not repeated information.
findings.failure_scenario: A player with no actions left in the afternoon calls Echoes twenty times from the browser console: each answer names a room, the ties come out one after another, and the GMs see nothing but twenty log lines 'Echoes for Aiko from Library: ...'.
findings.expected: The price of a paid act with no roll is judged where the act is judged, as the Frisk ask's is: the primary claims the payment's ticket (or spends the action itself) before it answers, and refuses `notPaid` with none.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a GM-side read of the payment on every road of the answer: echoesFor and echoesRefusal (echoes-gm.mjs:95-127) read the phase, the incident, the death and the map only; handleEchoes (bridge-runs-acts.mjs:327-334) passes the actor alone; no guard of the row reads actions; `git grep -i echoes` in roll-draw.mjs, sheet-audit.mjs and actions.mjs finds nothing, so no ticket kind names it. The sheet audit cannot help: not spending is no write. The trust model's 'What stays open' (.claude/rules/trust-model.md) speaks of a payment a console makes and hands back around a drawn roll, not of a no-roll act served with no payment at all; docs/dev/e69/STATUS.md 'What a console can still do' does not list it. Scenario 30's E69 part (30-security.mjs:6948-6958) forges Echoes only for another player's character; scenario 33's E69-C (33-bridge-paths.mjs:2002-2062) drives the paid legal road. Not run.

findings.title: A GM's own Infiltrate and room actions run on that GM's browser even when it is not the primary, while their GM halves are written 'on the primary GM'
findings.where: scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:58-149 (requestFacilityUse, requestDoorShut, requestDoorForce, requestDoorPick, requestDoorKnock, requestWatchDeclare, requestTailStart, requestEavesdrop, requestEavesdropStop, requestEchoes, requestMaskReveal, requestDash: `local` with no `onPrimary`); against scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:221-253, 276-284, 1086-1105, 1177-1240 (the passages, the lair and the Frisk rows, which pass `onPrimary: true`); scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1947 (the waiter runs `local` on any GM unless `onPrimary`)
findings.what_happens: `createWaiter.request` runs a request's `local` on any GM's browser, and asks the primary only where the asker passed `onPrimary` (bridge-guards.mjs:1947). The twelve asks of E69, E74 and E93 pass `local` alone, so on an Assistant GM (or any second GM) a press of the Infiltrate tile or a room action for a character runs doors-gm.mjs `shutDoor`, watch-gm.mjs `declareWatch`, tail-gm.mjs `startTail`, eavesdrop-gm.mjs `startEavesdrop`/`endEavesdrop`, facilities-gm through `handleFacilityUse` on that browser. Each of those says it runs 'on the primary GM' (doors-gm.mjs:99, watch-gm.mjs:59, tail-gm.mjs:5 and 58, eavesdrop-gm.mjs:14 and 109), and some of their work is gated on `isPrimaryGm()` there: `endEavesdrop` gives the listener's microphone back through `settleBlock` (eavesdrop-gm.mjs:154), which returns null off the primary (209-213), and the row's `changed` fires its hook and schedules the voice pass on the browser that wrote (216-220), so on a second GM the primary learns of the end only through the store's merge; and `handleFacilityUse` holds its once-a-time-of-day check in `serialWrite`, one browser's queue (bridge-runs-acts.mjs:121), so a use on the second GM and a player's use on the primary are not ordered against each other. The E79/E80/E91 rows beside them chose `onPrimary` for the same kind of world write.
findings.failure_scenario: With two GMs at the table, the Assistant GM presses 'Stop listening' for a student it is playing: the eavesdrop row ends, but the microphone block is settled only if the primary reacts to the store's change, which this road does not ask of it.
findings.expected: One writer for each of these records, as the passages' and the Frisk's asks have: `onPrimary: true` on the twelve asks, or a note beside each saying why a second GM's own client may write it.
findings.refutation_tried: Read each GM half for a primary check of its own: shutDoor, declareWatch, startTail and startEavesdrop have none (they write GM stores, which every GM holds and the engine merges, so the write itself is not lost); endEavesdrop's settleBlock is primary-only (eavesdrop-gm.mjs:209-213), and the primary's voice pass reads every row when it runs (`voiceTargets`, 178-181), so it may catch up on its next pass. Whether the primary reacts to a store change from another GM by settling the voices was not traced (voice.mjs not read), nor whether any GM-side caller presses these for a student in practice; a GM's own NPC is the usual case. No test found that drives these asks from a second GM (33-bridge-paths runs an Assistant GM for other rows).

findings.title: `remnant.edit` and `project.unsabotage` can never be carried out: the rows are a GM's alone and only a player's browser ever asks them
findings.where: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:807-823 and 858-873 (gmOnly rows); scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:561-570 and 660-667 (requestUndoSabotage, requestRemnantEdit); their only callers, scripts/projects.mjs:2357-2361 and scripts/remnants.mjs:2513-2517, behind `if (!game.user.isGM)`
findings.what_happens: Since E08+E28 C8 both rows refuse a player with 'an undo is the GM's own Reroll's'. Their asks are called from one place each, `undoSabotage` and `retuneRemnant`, and only on a player's browser; a GM, the primary or not, takes the local branch of both functions (projects.mjs:2363 on, remnants.mjs:2519 on), and every caller of those functions found is GM-side (reroll.mjs:1436, 2020, 2032; handover.mjs:754-755; cleanup-reshape.mjs:383; cleanup.mjs:2153). So `handleRemnantEdit` and `handleUnsabotage` run only for a forged packet, and the `sender.isGM &&` test at bridge-runs-records.mjs:337 is always true where it runs. The asks' comments still describe the old road: requestRemnantEdit 'a reroll has changed how well they hid it' (bridge-asks.mjs:660-664), requestUndoSabotage 'It is only ever called by Reroll' (561-567), while the Reroll calls `undoSabotage` on the GM.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer reads requestUndoSabotage's comment, adds a player-side caller expecting the thaw to land, and every call is refused 'Only the GM can take a result back'.
findings.expected: The two player branches and their asks gone (the rows kept for the refusal the suite reads), or the comments saying that the road is a refusal kept for 30-security.
findings.refutation_tried: `git grep -n 'retuneRemnant\|undoSabotage('` over scripts/ (tests left out) lists every caller; each is in a GM-only function or behind isGM. The rows stay meaningful as refusals: 30-security forges them (the row comments say so), so the declarations are not dead, only their run.

findings.title: A Hope Call's approval card prints the packet's Call name and effect, and no guard holds the key to a Call that waits for a GM
findings.where: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:628-639 (`call.approve`: knownSender, notSpectator, owns); scripts/call-gm.mjs:238-243 (title from `call?.label ?? payload.callLabel`, body from `payload.effect`)
findings.what_happens: The row judges only that the sender owns the character. The run puts on every GM's card the title from HOPE_CALLS when the key is known and the packet's `callLabel` when it is not, and always the packet's `effect` line (escaped). So a console can raise an approval card for a key that is no Call, or for a real Call with an effect line that is not the table's ('a free critical' under Experience). Nothing is armed beyond the table: an unknown key is refused at `call.arm` (call-effects.mjs `playerArmRefusal`/`ownArmRefusal`), and an approved key arms the table's `grants`; the card is a text the GM rules on as if the module wrote it.

findings.failure_scenario: A player's console asks approval of 'Experience' with the effect 'roll with advantage and a free critical'; the GM reads the module's card, approves, and the roll gets the Experience bonus alone.
findings.expected: The card's title and effect from the GM's own table (as its cost already is since E02), and the row refusing a key that is not a Hope Call waiting for a GM's yes.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the cost line: it comes from HOPE_CALLS since E02 (call-gm.mjs:229-243), so the pattern exists; the label and the effect did not follow it. Checked what an approval buys: guardArmGmYes keys the yes by Call key and the arm takes the table's grants (bridge-runs-records.mjs:515-521), so no rule is broken - only the GM's card text. Escaping holds (`esc`, `callGm` escapes the title).

findings.title: `notPaid` tells a player 'You haven't paid for that roll with an action' where the price was Hope or Sanity, and for a Frisk ask, which has no roll

Wykonaj akcję jeszcze raz.'); scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:391; scripts/roll-draw.mjs:1179 (drawRefusal) and scripts/frisk.mjs:802 (askToFrisk); scripts/config.mjs:1454-1470 (PRICE_CHAINS: an Analyze or an Objection paid with Hope or Sanity past its first step)

findings.title: Every chat message rendered on a GM's browser starts a dynamic import of messenger-app.mjs before it is asked whether it is a ruling card
findings.what_happens: The second renderChatMessageHTML hook runs `import("./messenger-app.mjs")` for each message drawn on any GM, and only inside the `.then` reads `cardFlag(message, "callCard")` and queries for `[data-drpg-call]`. The hook above it (136-142) asks its flag first and imports only for a held Key fee's card. The comment explains why the button query waits for the microtask (the secret swap draws the words in the same dispatch); the `callCard` flag test does not need to wait. A module already loaded is a cache hit, so the cost is a promise and a microtask per message, paid for the whole log at every load.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM loads a world with a 500-message log: 500 import promises and querySelector calls run during the log's draw, for the few cards that hold a ruling.
findings.expected: The cheap flag read before the import, or one shared resolved module reference; measured with game.drpg.counters() if it matters.
findings.refutation_tried: Foundry draws the log in batches, and a cached import() is fast; no frame time is claimed. Counts of work only, not measured.

by_decision.what: Echoes leaves out a body nobody has found, so a player who knows a classmate's token stands one door away and hears a farther room (or nobody) learns that classmate does not count - a death the GMs keep is one of the reasons.
by_decision.source: scripts/echoes-gm.mjs:10-13 ('WHO COUNTS (the owner's 10.11 (b)): ... no body (dead as the GMs hold it, a secret death too)'; 'Read here, on the GM, because a player's browser does not know a death the GMs keep'). Every browser holds the tokens (.claude/rules/trust-model.md, Listen's lines), so the inference is open to an honest player too; finding 1 makes it repeatable for free.

by_decision.what: Player text on the bridge carries no length bound in the whitelist (`as.text`): a Dynamic action's description, a Hope Call's note and effect, an Observe's request, a parked murder's and a betrayal's note reach the GMs' cards uncut, while the pre-session note and card.post are held to MAX_PLAYER_BYTES (pre-session-note.mjs:148-150, secret.mjs cardTooLong).
by_decision.source: scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1502-1503 ('No length bound is added to text: a bound could cut a note a player wrote honestly, and E43's fuzz stage owns it'); E43 is unshipped (tools/stages.json).

by_decision.what: A roll is spent when the run refuses after the roll was claimed (a facility already used, a Listen roll below the band, a discard in the Class Trial).
by_decision.source: scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1564-1568 ('a run that then refuses has spent the roll as it spent the dice'); bridge-runs-records.mjs:131-135.

by_decision.what: A GM's yes for an Experience or Ultimate is used up by `guardArmGmYes` before `guardArmLiving` asks about the beneficiary, so a Call refused for a body nobody found has spent its yes.
by_decision.source: scripts/bridge-guards.mjs:1081-1084 ('Asked after the buyer's own refusals ... and before `guardArmLiving`, which stays last') and 986-992 (rule D asked last so the two answers differ only where the living one is armed).

by_decision.what: A queued declaration (`queue: "project"`) is acknowledged on arrival, before its guards, and so answers `reply` only.
A Work's trace takes the band its packet names, and a console that sends no `remnant.place` leaves no trace.
A forged `free` crisis claim is scored as a failure, not refused.
With no GM connected, every request is refused before it is sent (`noGm`), never broadcast.

l1.settles_if: Hope down by twice the cost with one Call armed: a new finding; down by one cost: nothing to report
